Ingredient.name: Moringa Leaf
Ingredient.description: Hand-picked leaflets of Moringa oleifera, dried in a controlled low-temperature closed chamber to keep the leaf green rather than khaki.

Ingredient.name: Moringa Seed
Ingredient.description: The winged seed from the mature pod. Cold-pressed for its oil, or milled whole for capsules.

Ingredient.name: Moringa Flower
Ingredient.description: Cream-white blossoms gathered in the short flowering window and dried the same day.

Ingredient.name: Moringa Gum (Gond)
Ingredient.description: Resin that sets on the bark of the tree, collected by hand and milled.

Ingredient.name: Drumstick Pod
Ingredient.description: The green pod of the same tree, pulped for soups and mixes.

Ingredient.name: Amla
Ingredient.description: Indian gooseberry, dried and powdered, blended with moringa leaf.

Ingredient.name: Sprouted Millets
Ingredient.description: Multi-grain millet base, sprouted before roasting.

Faq.question: What exactly is moringa?
Faq.answer: Moringa oleifera Lam. (family Moringaceae) the drumstick tree, murungai in Tamil is a fast-growing, drought-resistant tree cultivated widely across Tamil Nadu. Its leaf is recognised among the most nutrient-dense plant foods on the planet: a good source of iron, calcium, potassium and beta-carotene, and a complete plant protein carrying all nine essential amino acids. Dried properly, the leaf retains that nutrition for years without refrigeration. Five parts of the tree enter our range leaf, pod, flower, seed and gum each processed differently into a different product.

Faq.question: Why does MiracleTree make such a point about drying?
Faq.answer: Because drying is where most moringa is lost. Fresh leaf is highly perishable, and uncontrolled conventional drying costs it colour, sensory quality and nutritional characteristics. So drying became our engineering problem: ULTCD (2014) moved the leaf into a controlled low-temperature closed chamber, and CLHPD (2019) extended controlled low-heat drying to premium moringa and other herbs. Everything else in our chain milling, formulation, packaging is built around protecting what drying preserves.

Faq.question: Which product should I start with?
Faq.answer: Most people start with either the Moringa Leaf Powder, if they cook, or the Moringa Tablets, if they would rather not think about it each morning. If you want the gentlest introduction, start with one of the teas.

Faq.question: Are your products vegetarian?
Faq.answer: Everything in the range is vegetarian apart from the Colostrum Protein Bar, which contains bovine colostrum. Each product page lists what is inside it.

Faq.question: How much should I take each day?
Faq.answer: Follow the serving stated on the pack. If you are pregnant, nursing, taking prescribed medication or managing a health condition, speak to your doctor before adding any supplement to your routine.

Faq.question: Can I cook with the leaf powder?
Faq.answer: Yes. Stir it into dal, rasam, chapati dough, smoothies or curd rice. Add it towards the end of cooking rather than at the start, so it keeps its colour.

Faq.question: How should I store these products?
Faq.answer: Keep every pack sealed, in a cool dry place, away from direct sunlight. Powders and teas do not need refrigeration. Use the oil within six months of opening.

Faq.question: What does shipping cost?
Faq.answer: Shipping is free on orders above ₹699. Below that a flat ₹60 applies. We ship across India.

Faq.question: How long will my order take?
Faq.answer: Orders are packed within one to two working days. Delivery usually takes three to seven working days depending on your pin code.

Faq.question: How do I track my order?
Faq.answer: Sign in and open Account → Orders. Once your parcel is handed to the courier, the tracking number appears there and in your confirmation email.

Faq.question: Can I return a product?
Faq.answer: Because these are agricultural food products, we cannot accept returns once an order has been delivered. If something arrives damaged or incorrect, email support@miracletree.in within 48 hours of delivery with photographs and we will make it right.

Faq.question: Which payment methods do you accept?
Faq.answer: Cards, UPI, net banking and wallets through our payment gateway, and cash on delivery where available for your pin code.

Faq.question: Do you add preservatives or colouring?
Faq.answer: No. The leaf powders and teas are single-ingredient. Where a product is a blend, every component is printed on the pack and listed on its product page.

Faq.question: Do you supply in bulk or wholesale?
Faq.answer: Yes. Bulk and export enquiries are handled through indiamoringa.com, or write to info@miracletree.in.

Milestone.title: The Moringa journey begins
Milestone.body: MiracleTree begins with a 100% focus on moringa: sustainable, organic-oriented cultivation, and a plan to find out what the whole tree is actually capable of. From the farm, the journey began.

Milestone.title: Rethinking moringa cultivation
Milestone.body: Field-level R&D across four cultivation systems — 12×12 ft, 8×8 ft, 4×4 ft, and high density at up to roughly 3,800 plants an acre. There is no single correct way to plant moringa — it depends on the farmer's purpose, local conditions and intended end product: leaf, biomass or tree development.

Milestone.title: Farmer education and knowledge transfer
Milestone.body: The farm opens to growers, who visit to observe the planting models side by side and adapt them. Practices are written up as SOPs so the knowledge travels. According to the company's industry records, moringa under cultivation in Tamil Nadu grew from roughly 1,800 acres in 2010 to around 9,000 by 2017. Demonstrate, educate, transfer, grow.

Milestone.title: ULTCD drying technology
Milestone.body: Ultra Low Temperature Closed Chamber Drying: controlled, low-temperature, closed-chamber dehydration in place of less controlled conventional drying. This is the point the company moved from moringa farming into moringa processing technology.

Milestone.title: Moringa enters modern functional food
Milestone.body: A moringa-leaf-loaded energy bar, introduced at Agri Intex in Coimbatore and later developed into MOGO®. Moringa leaf becomes a nutritional ingredient and then a ready-to-eat food. From farm to bar.

Milestone.title: Moringa becomes skin food
Milestone.body: Beauty Drops, developed from cold-pressed moringa seed oil, take the work past nutrition and into natural personal care, proving the seed had real commercial value beyond conventional agricultural use.

Milestone.title: CLHPD processing technology
Milestone.body: Controlled Low Heat Process Drying, built on the low-temperature work and developed for premium moringa and herbal materials. ULTCD to CLHPD: the next stage in controlled dehydration.

Milestone.title: Filler-free moringa supplements
Milestone.body: Filler-free tablets made from moringa leaf, flower and seed — part of a larger principle of creating value from several parts of the same tree.

Milestone.title: Building the moringa product ecosystem
Milestone.body: Product R&D accelerates across categories. The portfolio grows past powders and tablets into functional foods, energy bars, beverages, soups, tea, supplements, dried foods, seed products, cold-pressed oil, personal care and nutritional formulations — a farm-to-finished-product platform rather than a producer.

Milestone.title: Moringa enters corporate nutrition
Milestone.body: Energy-bar capability moves into larger-volume corporate requirements, including supplies associated with PayPal India. Moringa shifts from a specialist health-food concept into a format that can serve workplaces and large consumer groups.

Milestone.title: 35,000 moringa energy bars
Milestone.body: A manufacturing milestone: approximately thirty-five thousand bars produced for an Isha Life requirement — years of R&D translated into commercial-scale food manufacturing.

Milestone.title: 60+ moringa innovations
Milestone.body: More than fifteen years after the first planting, the portfolio reaches 60+ moringa products, formulations and product concepts across food, nutrition, wellness, supplements, beverages, personal care and ingredients. One tree, translated.

Milestone.title: Taking moringa knowledge global
Milestone.body: The work expands past exporting product. Experience in cultivation, high-density farming, nursery development, processing, value addition and commercial-scale project development begins contributing to international moringa projects. Products and activities have now reached 14+ countries.

Milestone.title: Building the moringa economy
Milestone.body: The journey continues across sustainable farming, farmer empowerment, processing technology, food and nutrition innovation, whole-tree value addition and global moringa projects — the next generation of moringa.

Leader.bio: He developed the two drying technologies the company is built on, ULTCD and CLHPD, and now leads MiracleTree's international moringa projects: technology transfer with NADEC in Saudi Arabia, and a 1.7-million-tree development at Thumrait in Oman.
Leader.longBio:
THE ENGINEER WHO NEVER SET OUT TO FARM

Saravanakumaran Rajendran grew up in Madurai in a household where both the table and the bookshelf were fed by the land. The meals were farm-fresh produce; the reading was Sangam literature. "My father made sure we learnt and appreciated Purananuru and Agathyan's writings," he recalls. Somewhere along the way, he admits, it all took a backseat.

He left with an engineering degree and went to work on the technology side of agriculture finding ways and means to make sustainable technology work for farming. "Solving problems was my goal, not farming," he smiles. Those years were spent on the equipment and process side of the field: the machines, the drying, the handling the unglamorous half of agriculture that decides whether a harvest survives.

The turn came in 2007, when a friend took him and his wife Sujatha to a three-day workshop with organic farming scientist G. Nammalwar. "He awakened the farmer within me," Kumaran says. It changed his outlook on agriculture entirely from purely commercial, to using his skills and education to help farmers utilise technology for sustainable farming.

The moringa idea was Sujatha's. In markets saturated with chemically grown produce, she wanted healthy, nutritional food to reach people as food they would buy anyway not capsules. When sustained production demanded technical and engineering support, he joined her. In 2009, the family's dedicated Moringa journey began.

He can still quote the Sangam couplet his father taught him as a child "Murungai undavan, verungai povaan." It is often misread as "the one who eats moringa will go empty-handed." The true meaning, he explains, is the opposite: the one who eats moringa will not need a walking stick towards the end of his life. The literature the young engineer set aside became the crop he now builds his life around.

The MiracleTree® family did not set out to simply farm; they sought to solve the processing side of agriculture. Recognising early that consumers needed convenient formats, the company moved Moringa beyond capsules and powders into everyday foods like bars, teas, and multigrain mixes.

The hard part is drying. Fresh Moringa is highly perishable, and inappropriate drying adversely affects colour and quality. In 2014, the company introduced ULTCD (Ultra Low Temperature Closed Chamber Drying), followed in 2019 by CLHPD (Controlled Low Heat Process Drying). Both are now applied to other herbs and vegetables.

The farm was run as a learning ground. Four planting models were trialled 12×12 ft, 8×8 ft, 4×4 ft, and high density (3,800 plants/acre) then organised into SOPs and shared with visiting farmers. During this period, MiracleTree® observed Moringa cultivation in Tamil Nadu grow from roughly 1,800 acres in 2010 to 9,000 by 2017.

Since 2021, the work has been international. MiracleTree® transferred expertise to NADEC in Saudi Arabia (2021–2023) and became a technology partner for an integrated campus at Thumrait, Oman (2025–2026) featuring 580 acres, 1.7 million trees, and a 44-tonne/day processing facility. The company's core principle remains: develop the system, document the SOP, train the team, and transfer the technology to build local capability rather than create dependency.
Leader.quote: Using the yield of the moringa tree was my wife Sujatha's brainchild. She wanted to reach healthy and chemical-free food to people.

Leader.name: Sujatha Rajendran
Leader.bio: Sujatha came up with the products. Her rule was that moringa had to arrive as food people already eat, not as a supplement, and the range still follows it.
Leader.longBio:
Sujatha Rajendran started the product side of the company. Her question was a commercial one: how do you get moringa to people who would never buy a supplement?

The answer was to make things they already eat. An energy bar instead of a capsule. Tea instead of a tincture. Laddus. The range still works to that rule, and it is the reason the company makes food rather than extracts.
